title: CSCI 220: Operating Systems
text:
CSCI 220: Operating Systems
Sample University, Department of Computer Science
Term: Fall 2026

Instructor: Dr. Imaginary Person (fictional)

Course description
This course explains how an operating system manages a computer: processes, scheduling, memory, files and concurrency.

Topics
1. Processes and threads: what a process is, process states, context switching, threads vs processes.
2. CPU scheduling: first-come-first-served, shortest job first, round robin, priority scheduling.
3. Synchronization: race conditions, locks, semaphores, deadlock.
4. Memory management: paging, virtual memory, page replacement.
5. File systems: files and directories, allocation methods, journaling.
Prerequisites for this course: you should understand recursion and linked lists from CSCI 201.

Grading
Assignment 1 (Process simulator): 10%, due Friday, November 13, 2026 at 11:59 PM
Assignment 2 (Scheduler): 10%, due Friday, November 27, 2026 at 11:59 PM
Quiz 1 (processes and scheduling): 5%, in class on Wednesday, November 11, 2026
Midterm exam: 25%, Thursday, November 19, 2026, 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM
Assignment 3 (Virtual memory): 10%, due Friday, December 4, 2026 at 11:59 PM
Final exam: 40%, date set by the registrar during the December exam period

Policies
Late work loses 10% per day. The lowest quiz mark is dropped.

concepts.label: Process and process states
concepts.summary: A process is a running program that moves through states such as ready, running and waiting.

concepts.label: Context switching
concepts.summary: The OS saves one process's state and loads another's so the CPU can be shared.

concepts.label: Threads vs processes
concepts.summary: Threads share a process's resources while processes are isolated from each other.

concepts.label: First-come-first-served
concepts.summary: Scheduling policy that runs jobs in the order they arrive.

concepts.label: Shortest job first
concepts.summary: Scheduling policy that runs the job with the shortest run time next.

concepts.label: Round robin
concepts.summary: Each job gets a fixed time slice in turn.

concepts.label: Priority scheduling
concepts.summary: The job with the highest priority runs first.

concepts.label: Race conditions
concepts.summary: Bugs where the result depends on the unpredictable timing of concurrent operations.

concepts.label: Locks
concepts.summary: Mechanisms that let only one thread enter a critical section at a time.

concepts.label: Semaphores
concepts.summary: Counters used to control access to shared resources and to coordinate threads.

concepts.label: Deadlock
concepts.summary: A state where processes wait on each other forever and none can proceed.

concepts.label: Paging
concepts.summary: Memory is divided into fixed-size pages mapped to physical frames.

concepts.label: Virtual memory
concepts.summary: Gives each process a large private address space backed by RAM and disk.

concepts.label: Page replacement
concepts.summary: Rules for choosing which page to evict when memory is full.

concepts.label: Files and directories
concepts.summary: How the OS names, organizes and stores data on disk.

concepts.label: Allocation methods
concepts.summary: Ways of laying out file blocks on disk, such as contiguous, linked or indexed.

concepts.label: Journaling
concepts.summary: Logging changes before applying them so the file system can recover after a crash.

concepts.label: Recursion and linked lists
concepts.summary: CSCI 201 prerequisite knowledge assumed for this course.
